title: the right operand of instanceof selects a prototype and reads no host state
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Host Globals': "Facilities truly present in every supported JavaScript environment MAY be unconditional globals. Host-sensitive operations such as clock and random access MUST still use capabilities." The rule is therefore per-OPERATION, not per-object — the same distinction 20-host-globals/universal-globals-stay-available pins for `Math.max` beside `Math.random`. `Date.parse`, `Date.UTC` and `new Date(<authored instant>)` were already exempt on exactly that reasoning; `instanceof` selects a prototype and reads no clock, and the form was simply missed. Both backends charged SMITHERS1602 here until 2026-08-25. `new Date(0)` on line 2 is the already-exempt authored-instant form and doubles as this case's own control. The refusal half is 20-host-globals/the-date-constructor-in-a-value-position-is-still-charged.
